g.text: Legacy build: MAX7219 8-digit module via 74AHCT125 buffer on a breadboard (SPI0), panel button
Raspberry Pi 5 / Pi 4. Physical header pin numbers, BCM GPIO names. Power off before wiring. Source: hardware/SPEC.md §3.1, §3.4, §3.5
Wire colours: red 5 V · black GND · grey SPI MOSI to DIN · violet (purple) SPI SCLK to CLK · brown SPI CE0 to CS · green panel button (GPIO17)
C2 (100 nF) decouples U1: its legs go straight into the breadboard rows of U1 pins 14 and 7 (dashed lines = no wire).
The MAX7219 needs 3.5 V logic-high: its DIN, CS and CLK connect only to U1 outputs, never to the Pi.

g.title: PI
g.text: Only the pins used by this build are shown.

g.title: W1
g.text: F on the Pi, M into the breadboard row of the U1 pin

g.title: W3
g.text: Dupont jumper F-F, far housing cut off
Female housing on the Pi. Button end: strip 5 mm,
solder to the lug under 4.8 mm heat-shrink, or clamp in the screw terminal.

g.title: U1
g.text: Powered from 5 V; TTL inputs accept 3.3 V logic.
All four OE (active low) and the unused 4A tied to GND.

g.title: C2
g.text: Legs bent over the chip; keep them short.

g.title: W2
g.text: M into the breadboard row of the U1 pin, F on the MAX7219

g.title: L1
g.text: All six links to the same GND rail

g.title: BUTTON
g.text: Panel button, 16 mm momentary, normally open
2-lug switch - either way round. 3-lug switch - use C and NO, leave NC free.
